title: Project
description: One video: its script, what each line shows, and the cuts made from it.

captions.description: How captions are cut into cues.

cuts.description: The videos made from the script.

errata.description: Corrections to what a published video says, by line.

expectations.description: Text that must be on screen when a scene is captured.

lines.description: The script: every narrated line, in order.

publish.description:
What goes with the video where it is uploaded: its description,
tags, links, titles and thumbnails.

scenes.description: What the lines show, by ID.

sections.description: The sections, by ID. They come in the order of their first line.

voice.description: The voices that speak the lines.

Action.description:
One step on a web page. Exactly one verb is set: `click`, `select`,
`expand`, `collapse`, `scroll`, `scroll_to` or `wait`, each naming a target.

collapse.description: Close the target if it is open, by clicking `control`.

control.description: For `expand` and `collapse`: the CSS selector, inside the target, to click.

expand.description: Open the target if it is closed (`aria-expanded`), by clicking `control`.

offset.description: For `scroll_to`: the gap left above the target, in CSS pixels.

scroll.description: Scroll the target, a scroll container, to `top`.

scroll_to.description: Scroll `within` until the target is at its top, less `offset`.

top.description: For `scroll`: the scroll position, in CSS pixels.

wait.description: Wait until the target is visible.

within.description: For `scroll_to`: the scroll container, a target.

matches.description: A regular expression its value must match.

Camera.description: A named framing of a web scene.

union.description: Frame the union of these targets.

vertical.description: The camera vertical cuts use instead, when this one is too wide.

Captioning.description: How captions are cut into cues (TODO.md, P6-VIDNI-05).

Captions.description: How a cut carries its captions.

oneOf.description: A clean picture, with captions as SRT and VTT files.
A clean master with caption files, and a burned-in variant.

ColorScheme.description: A colour scheme a web scene can ask for.

Cut.description: A video made from the script.

end_hold.description:
How long a 16:9 cut holds its last picture after the narration
ends, in seconds from 5 to 20, for an end screen to go over. It
takes the place of `timing.tail` in this cut.

id.description: A stable ID, like a line's.

language.description:
The language the cut speaks, when it isn't the script's: a dubbed
cut. Its lines show and say their `in.<language>` words, and its
narration is the takes of those words.

lines.description: `all`, or the IDs of the lines the cut uses, in script order.

platforms.description:
The platform profiles the cut is made for. Default: `youtube` for
16:9; `youtube-shorts`, `instagram-reels` and `whatsapp-status` for 9:16.

size.description: The frame size in pixels. Default `[1920, 1080]` or `[1080, 1920]`.

swap.description:
Scenes this cut shows in the place of others, as `shown = "instead"`:
where a line shows the scene `shown`, or lays it over its picture,
this cut has the scene `instead`. So a short can have a narrower
terminal, or an overlay with fewer parts, under the same lines.

Erratum.description:
A correction to what a line says, made after the video was published
(TODO.md, P6-VIDNI-07). It goes into the description of every cut that
uses the line, and changes no picture.

on.description: The day of the correction, as `2026-11-20`.

Expectation.description: Text a web scene must show, checked when it is captured.

at.description: `setup`, or the ID of a line on that scene: checked after its actions.

target.description: The target whose text is read.

text.description: The text of the target's single match.

texts.description: The texts of all its matches, in page order.

Grow.description: How a match grows to its enclosing block.

margin.description: The block must stay this many CSS pixels narrower than the container.

max_height.description: The tallest block it may grow to, in CSS pixels.

within.description: The container the match grows within (a CSS selector).

HeardAs.description:
One word as the listening check hears it, and the script's word for
the same sound.

heard.description: The word as whisper writes it. Case is ignored.

camera.description:
The web scene's camera for landscape cuts; the scene's
`default_camera` when absent.

camera_vertical.description: The camera for vertical cuts, when it differs.

claim.description:
Whether the line states a fact. In strict projects, every line that
does needs a `source`; set `claim = false` on a line that states none,
such as a greeting or a transition.

do.description: Actions on a web scene before the line is captured.

highlight.description: Targets of a web scene to box while the line plays.

id.description: A stable ID: lowercase letters and digits in words joined by hyphens.

in.description:
The line's words in other languages, by language: `in.ta.show`.
A cut with `language = "ta"` shows and says these.

only.description:
The cuts the line is only for, such as a short's hook. A cut that
uses every line leaves out the lines that are only for others.

overlay.description: A page scene drawn over the line's picture.

say.description: What is said, when it differs from what is shown.

scene.description: The scene the line shows; `meta.default_scene` when absent.

section.description: The section the line belongs to.

show.description: The caption: the line as it is shown.

source.description: Where the line's facts come from.

LineSelection.description: "all", or the IDs of the lines a cut uses.

label.description: What the link is, such as `The code`.

url.description: Where it goes: an `http` or `https` address.

banned.description:
Regular expressions, matched without regard to case, that no line may
show or say.

default_scene.description: The scene a line shows when it names none.

in.description:
The title and subtitle in other languages, by language, for the
cuts that speak them.

language.description: The script's language, as a BCP 47 tag.

strict.description: Whether every factual line must name its source (P2-VIDNI-06).

subtitle.description: A short line shown with the title, such as a series name.

MetaWords.description: A video's title in another language.

library.description: The tracks the project may use, each with its licence.

track.description: `none`, or the ID of a track in `library`.

under.description: How far under the narration the track plays, in LU. Default 20.

PageSize.description: A page scene's size for each orientation, in pixels.

Part.description: One part of an overlay: a chip, a box, or a wall between boxes.

label.description: A chip's word, or a box's small heading.

sign.description: A chip's sign, before its word: one character, such as `?`.

text.description: The line under a chip's word, or a box's words.

tone.description: The colour of a chip's sign and word, or of a box's top edge.

wall.description:
In a `flow`: a wall between the boxes before it and after it,
with these words on it. A wall has no other key.

Pick.description: Which of a target's matches to keep.

Publish.description:
What goes with the video where it is uploaded (TODO.md, P6-VIDNI-04).
None of it is in a picture, so changing it renders nothing again.

description.description:
The description: what the video is about, in your own words.
Chapters, links and credits are added after it.

links.description: Links to list under the description.

thumbnails.description:
Up to three thumbnails for a 16:9 cut, each a frame of a line.
With none, there is one: the cut's first line, with the title.

titles.description: The title on a platform, by profile ID, where it isn't `meta.title`.

Respelling.description: One text and how it is said.

by.description: card: whose words a `quote` card's are.

cameras.description: web: named framings. `viewport` and `highlights` are always defined.

color_scheme.description: web: the colour scheme the page is asked for.

columns.description:
terminal, code: how many characters wide the text is; a longer
line goes on in the next row. Default: 80 for a terminal, and the
longest line's length for code, between 40 and 100.

default_camera.description: web: the camera of a line that names none. Default `viewport`.

items.description: card: the points of a `bullets` card.

kind.description:
`web`: a page captured at a fixed viewport and framed by the virtual
camera. `page`: an HTML file rendered at each cut's own size, for
cards and overlays. `card`: a card drawn from one of the theme's
templates. `overlay`: a strip drawn over a line's picture, from a
template and the scene's `parts`. `image`: a picture in the project
folder, PNG or SVG, framed by the virtual camera. `terminal`: a transcript of commands
and what they printed, drawn as a terminal. `code`: an excerpt of
a source file, drawn with its syntax in colour.

language.description:
code: the language its syntax is coloured as. Default: by the
file's name.

lines.description:
terminal, code: the first and last line of the file to show,
counted from 1. Default: all of it.

parts.description: overlay: its chips, or its boxes and walls, in order.

prompt.description: terminal: what a command's line starts with. Default `$ `.

quote.description: card: the words of a `quote` card.

repo.description:
code: the git repository `rev` is in, from the project folder.
Default: the project folder's own.

rev.description:
code: the git revision the file is read at, as a commit's hash.
Without it the file is read as it is in the project folder.

scale.description:
web: device pixels per CSS pixel. Default 1. image, terminal,
code: how many times its own size the picture is drawn.

setup.description: web: actions run once, after the page loads.

size.description: page: the rendered size for each orientation. Default: the cut's size.

targets.description:
web: named parts of the page, for highlights, cameras, actions and
expectations.

template.description: card: the template it is drawn from.

title.description:
card: its title (`title`, `section`, `bullets`, `end`). terminal,
code: the words in the window's bar; default: the file's name.

transparent.description: page: rendered on a transparent background, as an overlay.

url.description:
web: the page's address. page: a file in the project folder;
`{aspect}` becomes `16x9` or `9x16`. image: the picture's file.
terminal: the transcript's file. code: the source file, in the
project folder, or in `repo` at `rev`.

vertical_follows_highlights.description:
web: in vertical cuts, a line whose highlights are at most this many
CSS pixels wide is framed on its highlights.

viewport.description: web: the viewport in CSS pixels. Default `[1280, 720]`.

SceneKind.description: The kinds of scene in schema 1.

Section.description: A run of lines under one label.

chapter.description:
The section's title in a chapter list, when it isn't the label.
Empty to stay in the chapter before.

in.description: The label in other languages, by language.

label.description:
Shown on screen while the section plays, and used for chapters. Empty
for none.

SectionWords.description: A section's label in another language.

Split.description: How a line's caption is cut into cues.

theme.description: `default`, or the path of a theme folder.

Target.description: A named part of a web page: the visible elements that match.

any.description: The union of other matchers, instead of `css`.

attr.description: Keep the elements whose attribute matches.

columns.description:
With `lines`: the first and last column of the window that the
target is, counted from 1. Default: the window's whole width.

exclude.description: Drop the elements whose text matches.

grow.description: Grow each match to its largest enclosing block that still ends with the same text.

line.description: One line of the element's text, counted from 0.

lines.description:
On a terminal or code scene: the first and last line of the file
that the target is, counted from 1.

merge.description: Draw one box around all the matches.

rect.description:
On an image scene: a part of the picture, as `[x, y, width,
height]` in its own pixels (an SVG's, in its own units).

text.description: Keep the elements whose text matches.

text_of.description: Match `text` against this child (a CSS selector) instead of the whole element.

unique.description: When reading texts, keep each text once.

Template.description: The templates a card scene is drawn from.

oneOf.description: A title and a subtitle: a video's opening card.
A section's name, with a line above it.
A title and a list of points.
A quotation, and whose it is.
A closing card: a title and a line under it, centred.
An overlay: a row of chips, each a sign, a word and a line under it.
An overlay: boxes joined by arrows, with walls between groups of them.
An overlay: one box of words.

TextMatch.description: A string to match exactly, after collapsing whitespace, or a table with one of starts_with, contains or matches.

TextRule.description: A text test other than an exact match. Exactly one key is set.

Thumbnail.description: A thumbnail: the picture of a line, with words over it.

line.description: The line whose picture it is.

title.description: The words drawn over the picture. Default: none.

Timing.description: The pauses around the lines, in seconds.

line_gap.description: The pause between two lines of one section.

Tone.description: What a part of an overlay is coloured as.

Track.description: A piece of music the project may use, with what allows it.

attribution.description: The credit the licence asks for, as it goes into a description.

content_id.description:
Whether the track is registered with YouTube's Content ID. A Short
over a minute with a Content ID claim is blocked worldwide.

file.description: The track's file in the project folder: a 16-bit WAV.

id.description: A stable ID, like a line's.

licence.description:
The licence it is used under, such as `CC-BY-4.0`, or the name of
a paid licence.

sha256.description: The file's SHA-256, so that the licence is of this very file.

Voice.description: The voices that speak the lines.

draft.description: The synthetic draft voice: a voice pack, as `<engine>:<model>`.

heard_as.description:
Words the listening check hears spelled differently from the script
for the same sound. They make its scores fairer and change nothing
else: no output depends on what the check hears.

in.description:
The draft voices of other languages, by language, for the cuts
that speak them.

length_scale.description: The draft voice's pace: above 1 is slower.

read_as.description:
How a reader says symbols that the captions show. The prompter shows
these, and takes are scored against them.

respell.description: Spellings the draft voice says better, applied in order to what it speaks.

seed.description:
Where a line's first draft takes its seeds from. The seed it keeps
goes into `voice.lock`, so changing this changes only the lines
drafted afresh.

VoiceIn.description: The draft voice of another language.

draft.description: The synthetic draft voice for this language, as `<engine>:<model>`.

Words.description: A line's words in another language.

say.description: What is said, when it differs from what is shown.

show.description: What the captions show, and what is said.
